text:
Recent work supports aligning collaborative and textual representations, but does not establish gains for a text encoder trained from scratch inside NextItNet. [TSSR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07623) uses item-level and user-level contrastive alignment; [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) uses semantic codes, selective text fusion and auxiliary masking objectives to address the textual–collaborative gap. These motivate selective integration rather than assuming semantic similarity equals next-item relevance. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns LLM-derived description embeddings with collaborative information; its pretrained features and Transformer backbone make it indirect evidence for the constrained setting.

Representation clustering is a concrete concern: [UniT (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13530) reports tighter semantic clusters among less-popular items and proposes sampling-dependent repulsion to improve uniformity. This differs from layerwise oversmoothing and does not establish that NextItNet suffers the same mechanism. A plausible experimental adaptation—not a published compatibility claim—is a small randomly initialized title/description encoder, gated into item-ID embeddings before NextItNet’s residual dilated causal convolutions, with weak item-level contrastive alignment and one jointly trained scoring head. Compare against ID-only and text-without-alignment controls; vary alignment weight, text dropout and gate strength. Measure representation cosine similarity/variance alongside macro validation HR@10 to detect collapse or harmful semantic dominance. Retain one checkpoint per category and final-nonpadding readout. No directly matching 2024–2026 from-scratch NextItNet result was identified in this search; artist, style or task compatibility should remain hypotheses unless supported by permitted metadata and validation.
